prompt.description: The user's onboarding request in natural language.

accelerator_type.description: The TPU type the onboarding targets: the accelerator label from tpu-agent's one `compute inspect` (`accelerator`, else `details.accelerator_type` or `details.tpu_accelerator`), e.g. tpu7x or tpu-v6e-slice, not the slice shape, which onboarding sizes itself. Onboarding compares generations, so tpu7x and v7x match. Required: when the probe finds none, tpu-agent asks the user rather than guessing from a profile, VM or cluster name.

model.description: Optional hint: target model specification (HF hub ID or local path).

local_path.description: Local checkpoint path if onboarding private weights.

task.description: Target pipeline tag or model architecture task.

mode.description: Optional. Omit only when tpu-agent could not resolve the user's intent; tpu-model-onboarding cannot ask, so an unset mode is a question its caller still owes. `candidate` is set only by tpu-agent's optimization-heuristics round: serve and benchmark a serving candidate tpu-diagnostics proposed, the way the baseline was, and compare the two (tpu-model-onboarding's Measuring a serving candidate).

compute_target.description: Optional compute runtime target (e.g. local, tpu-vm, gke-job).

servers.description: Optional: servers an earlier onboarding in this session left serving, each copied verbatim from that onboarding's result. A sweep of several shapes may measure on one whose deployments_json and launch_recipe files have the same contents as this deployment's, beside its own servers; it never cancels one.

profile.description: compute_profile from that result: the compute profile the server runs under.

deployments_json.description: output_files.deployments_json from the result that launched it.

launch_recipe.description: output_files.launch_recipe from the result that launched it.

checkpoint_bucket.description: Optional gs:// bucket for shared checkpoints: onboarding stages a Hugging Face model or local checkpoint directory there once (stage_checkpoint.py) and every job reads it from GCS instead of the Hub. On gke_job the pods must be able to read it (a pod_service_account, or the profile's own staging_bucket); otherwise, and by default, onboarding stages into the profile's staging_bucket.

examples.prompt: Benchmark meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on TPU against CPU.

Measure serving candidate m-tp2xdp4 against the baseline: serve /workspace/optimization-heuristics/changes/m-tp2xdp4/deployments.json, benchmark it with the baseline's bench_request at the baseline's points, and compare with the baseline summaries /workspace/bench/baseline_summary.json. Candidates: /workspace/optimization-heuristics/candidates.json.
